messages:
amy: Hey team — opening a quick coordination thread for the SDK snippet refresh in the streaming + pagination docs. PR is at https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482. I updated the Python example but want parity for TS/Go and a short migration note for users upgrading from stream_iter -> stream.

sasha: Thanks Amy. Quick read: your Python sample uses an async iterator pattern. Can we make the TS/Go examples show the equivalent streaming cursor + retry rather than a full iterator abstraction? Keeps them shorter for the docs. :+1:

miguel: I can take TS. Plan: show a small fetch loop with backoff and a tiny retry wrapper. Example idea:
```ts
// pseudo-TS streaming loop w/ retry
async function streamResponses(client) {
  let cursor = undefined
  while (true) {
    const res = await retry(() => client.stream({cursor}))
    for (const chunk of res.chunks) console.log(chunk.text)
    if (!res.nextCursor) break
    cursor = res.nextCursor
  }
}
```

rob: I can do Go. Keep it sync-friendly (channel-based streaming) and show how to re-open on transient errors. Example: read from a stream until EOF, re-establish with exponential backoff.

amy: Perfect. Two style notes: 1) call out that the new runtime returns "chunks" with optional nextCursor (not page_token) 2) tiny migration box: old stream_iter code snippet -> new stream loop (one-liner diff).

sasha: For the migration blurb, want a before/after with minimal code. Something like:
```py
# before (old helper)
for msg in client.stream_iter(prompt):
  print(msg.text)

# after (explicit cursor-based streaming)
cursor = None
while True:
  resp = client.stream(prompt, cursor=cursor)
  for chunk in resp.chunks: print(chunk.text)
  if not resp.next_cursor: break
  cursor = resp.next_cursor
```

miguel: I'll mirror the same concept in TS and call out the retry helper we use in examples (linear backoff, max 3 tries). Should we include the tiny helper in the snippet or point to the util?

rob: Include the minimal helper inline so readers don't need to jump. Keep it 8-10 lines.

amy: Great. One more ask: please add a short note under "Edge cases" about how to handle partial chunks (combine last token with next chunk) — a single sentence is enough.

sasha: Noted. I'll add that line and a link to the streaming decoding section.

miguel: Quick question about tests — do we want unit examples asserting the client replays after transient 5xx? I can add a tiny pytest for Python.

amy: Yes, add one smoke unit test that mocks a transient failure and ensures the loop resumes. Put it in tests/docs_snippets/test_stream_retry.py.

ci-bot: CI status for branch docs/snippet-stream-refresh: checks/linters OK, checks/markdown-link-check failed on docs/streaming.md line 214 (relative link).

amy: Thanks CI. I'll fix the link in the PR ASAP.

docs-bot: PR #482 updated: added TypeScript snippet + Go draft. Reviewer requested: @sasha.

sasha: I'll review today. If I find minor wording tweaks I'll push commits to the branch rather than requesting changes.

rob: Pushed the Go snippet as draft in the branch. Tests included for the retry helper.

amy: Awesome — merging plan: after Sasha review, squash & merge, then follow-up small patch for the markdown link and add the unittest path in the PR description.

miguel: Sounds good. If anyone wants me to compress the TS snippet further (remove the helper) I can, but I think inline is better for discoverability.

amy: Agreed. Thanks all — ping here once merged and I'll update the changelog entry under "SDK examples". :rocket:

(END)
